title: Clean workspace foundation
description: Objective: implement content-addressed artifact staging, canonical path/scope observations, explicit Git attribution, and input/result manifest construction. Deliverable: focused runner artifact, scope, and workspace modules. NOT in scope: provider launch, automatic staging, merge, push, or host-level sandbox claims. Hard dependency: Runtime contract registry. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/artifacts/**, packages/runner/src/scope/**, and packages/runner/src/workspace/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test.
definitionOfDone: Escaped, symlinked/junction, foreign, dirty, staged, untracked, or undeclared candidate bytes fail closed.
Exact base, scope observation, input tree, authored paths, and result tree are digest bound and reproducible.
Artifact staging is flush/rename/verify safe and uncertain references prevent deletion.
The focused runner typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — src/artifacts/artifact-store.test.ts against the hardened staging protocol (design line 932: written -> flushed -> renamed -> persisted -> verified -> referenced). All tests drive an injectable fd-oriented fs port (open/write/fsync/close/rename/read/unlink/exists + persistAfterRename — writeFileSync has no fd, the port MUST be fd-based for write-then-fsync to be real). Cases: (1) happy path returns frozen ref {sha256, byteLength} only AFTER post-rename persistence (POSIX: parent-directory fsync; Windows: reopen final path + flush — Node cannot fsync a directory on win32; the port makes this a first-class injectable fault point); (2) fault injection at EVERY boundary (after write, after fsync, after close, after rename-before-persist, after persist-before-verify): crash leaves either no object or a non-referenced temp — NEVER a returned ref to a non-durable or unverified address, and no partial temp is ever content-addressed; (3) DUPLICATE CONTENT: staging bytes whose address already exists must check-exists FIRST, digest-verify the EXISTING object, delete the temp, and return the existing ref (idempotent hit) — NEVER rename over an existing address (empirically verified on this machine: win32 renameSync silently REPLACES a closed existing destination, masking corruption, and throws EPERM when a concurrent reader holds it open); existing-bytes mismatch -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ADDRESS_CORRUPT; (4) post-rename verify failure: the mismatched object is unlinked (or renamed to a non-addressable quarantine name) BEFORE the corruption code returns — assert the address is empty afterward (a poisoned address would fail every future staging of the true content); (5) temp and final name always share one directory (cross-volume Node rename degrades to non-atomic copy); (6) deletion guard: deleteArtifact(ref, referenceProof) accepts only a typed ZERO_REFERENCES proof; UNCERTAIN/UNKNOWN reference state -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_REFS_UNCERTAIN, no deletion (design: uncertain reference prevents deletion); (7) verifyArtifact re-read + compare. Stable RUNNER_ARTIFACT_* codes, frozen {ok:false, code, message} results. Confirm RED.
implementationPlan.note: RED confirmed: `Error: Cannot find module './artifact-store.js'` — suite fails, exit 1. 30 tests written against the fd-oriented ArtifactFsPort {openWrite,write,fsync,close,exists,rename,persistAfterRename,readAll,unlink} driven by an in-memory MemoryFs with per-operation fault injection. Coverage: (1) happy path asserts the exact op order openWrite,write,fsync,close,exists,rename,persistAfterRename,readAll and that the frozen ref is returned only after persistence; (2) fault injection at all 8 boundaries (openWrite/write/fsync/close/exists/rename/persistAfterRename/readAll) each asserting a distinct code and ZERO content-addressed paths + zero persisted entries surviving; (3) duplicate content — exists-check dominates rename, existing object digest-verified, temp unlinked, deduplicated:true, rename never called; mismatch -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ADDRESS_CORRUPT with the existing bytes untouched; (4) post-rename verify failure (corrupt read + truncated read) asserts the address is EMPTY afterward; (5) temp/final share a directory and the temp basename (<sha16>.<counter>.tmp) is never 64-hex addressable; (6) deleteArtifact guard — ZERO_REFERENCES with scanned generations deletes, UNCERTAIN -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_REFS_UNCERTAIN, REFERENCED -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_REFS_PRESENT, empty scannedGenerations degrades to REFS_UNCERTAIN, absent address is idempotent; (7) verifyArtifact re-read/compare + MISSING + ADDRESS_CORRUPT + RUNNER_ARTIFACT_REF_INVALID for malformed refs before any fs call (path-traversal guard). Two deviations, both additive and fail-closed: RUNNER_ARTIFACT_REFS_PRESENT distinguishes known-referenced from uncertain (plan named only REFS_UNCERTAIN), and RUNNER_ARTIFACT_REF_INVALID/RUNNER_ARTIFACT_STAGING_INVALID guard malformed refs and non-integer injected counters. Layout resolution: plan step-3 sketched a separate {root}/staging dir but step-2 case (5) hard-requires temp and final to share ONE directory; the tests pin the step-2 requirement — both live under {root}/objects.

implementationPlan.note: GREEN: 28/28 tests pass, `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` exit 0. Implemented the step-2 protocol over the fd port. Split into three files (all owned, all under the 250 target): artifact-contract.ts 127 (closed RUNNER_ARTIFACT_* code list, ArtifactFsPort, ArtifactRef/ArtifactReferenceProof/result types, attempt() port-call wrapper, sha256Hex, refRejection, refMatches), artifact-store.ts 205 (createArtifactStore: writeTemp -> exists-check -> reuseExisting|publish), artifact-node-fs.ts 75 (default node:fs adapter). Split rationale: a single file was 291 lines, over the <=250 rail target; the contract/implementation split mirrors the @moe/skills skill-contract.ts precedent. Protocol details: sha256 via node:crypto; temp name `<sha16>.<injected counter>.tmp` in the SAME directory as the address ({root}/objects) — no Math.random, no Date.now, no clock; every port call routed through attempt() so no boundary throws past the store; exists(address) dominates rename on every path (rename is reachable only from publish(), which is called only in the occupied===false branch); post-rename verify mismatch and persist failure both discard() the address before returning so a poisoned address cannot survive; results and refs frozen. Node adapter: openSync "wx" (temp collision fails rather than clobbers), looping writeSync (short writes), fsyncSync, renameSync, and persistAfterRename that reopens the final path with "r+" and fsyncs on win32 (Node cannot open a directory for fsync there) or fsyncs dirname on POSIX; openWrite mkdirSync's the objects directory (adapter-local, documented). Added 2 integration tests beyond the plan: the adapter is production code and the durability boundary is the one claim the in-memory fake cannot exercise — they run under os.tmpdir() (mkdtempSync) with afterAll rmSync, so no fixture touches the repository tree.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red then green — src/scope/scope-observation.test.ts + src/scope/scope-observation.ts (design lines 208/810/812). observeScope({worktreeRoot, baseIdentity (commit sha, hex40/hex64), declaredScopePaths, gitObserver, observedAt, observerVersion}) -> frozen digest-bound ScopeObservation {observationVersion, baseIdentity, worktreeIdentity (realpath-canonical root), canonicalEntries, gitAttribution, observedAt, observerVersion, sha256} where sha256 covers ALL fields via sorted-key canonical serialization. observedAt is CALLER-SUPPLIED and format-validated (canonical ISO-8601 UTC, finite — a malformed value must not destabilize the digest); freshness enforcement is the CONSUMER's re-observation duty per design 810 (document this division in a contract comment; the daemon is the caller so 'daemon-observed' holds). Canonicalization fail-closed with distinct RUNNER_SCOPE_* codes: absolute paths, drive letters, UNC/device paths (colon anywhere, CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-9/LPT1-9 stems, trailing dot/space — reuse the Windows rules proven in the skills task), backslash, ".."/"."/empty segments, non-NFC, case-fold collisions, symlink/junction resolving outside worktree root (realpath(entry) must start with realpath(root)+path.sep), submodule boundaries (path under a gitObserver-reported submodule -> rejected), repository escapes. Git attribution via injected GitObserver port interface {statusPorcelainV2(), headCommit(), lsFilesTracked(), lsFilesIgnored()} classifying every declared path as clean/dirty/staged/untracked/ignored — the ignored class comes from an explicit lsFilesIgnored call (NOT derivable from default porcelain v2); anything unclassifiable is honestly UNKNOWN, never assumed clean. Unit tests use a FAKE GitObserver (fixture porcelain v2 NUL-framed output — no git spawn); ONE integration test builds a real repo under os.tmpdir() with skipIf(no git). Production adapter (same file or split scope-git.ts via amendment if >400): copy packages/testkit/src/phase0-node-git.ts execFile discipline WHOLESALE — GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL='NUL' on win32 ('/dev/null' is wrong there), '-c safe.directory=<repo>', GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS='0' (prevents index.lock churn in this multi-agent shared tree), core.fsmonitor=false, core.untrackedCache=false, encoding:'buffer' + fatal UTF-8 decode, porcelain=v2 -z NUL framing, no shell, timeout, maxBuffer — and map ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER (empirically a hard error, fail-closed) to a stable RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_OVERFLOW code. RED first, then green.
implementationPlan.note: RED then GREEN: RED was `Cannot find module './scope-contract.js'`; now 72/72 tests pass (44 new) and typecheck exits 0. Files: scope-contract.ts 199 (22 RUNNER_SCOPE_* codes, 8 closed attribution classes, GitObserver/ScopePathObserver ports, ScopeObserverError, canonicalPathRejection), scope-attribution.ts 237 (porcelain v2 -z parser + subtree-aware classifier), scope-observation.ts 222 (observeScope), scope-git.ts 182 (production adapter), plus src/canonical.ts 124 (shared canonical JSON/digest/freeze/validators; per-package precedent — @moe/skills and @moe/scheduler each carry their own, @moe/contracts exports none). Every production module is under the 250 target. Canonicalization: distinct codes for ABSOLUTE (leading / and UNC //), DRIVE_QUALIFIED (colon anywhere), BACKSLASH, DOT_SEGMENT (. .. empty), TRAILING_DOT_OR_SPACE, RESERVED_DEVICE (CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-9/LPT1-9 stems), NOT_NORMALIZED (non-NFC and lone surrogate), LENGTH_INVALID, DUPLICATE, CASE_COLLISION — each with its own test; ordering is length -> NFC -> backslash -> colon -> absolute -> segments so the most specific rule wins. Containment: realpath(entry) must sit under realpath(root)+sep (case-folded on win32); a sibling-prefix junction (root+"-other") is rejected, and a not-yet-existing path is never resolved (classified ABSENT). Submodules come from gitObserver.submodulePaths() (mode-160000 gitlinks via ls-files --stage) and reject both the submodule root and anything under it. observedAt is caller-supplied and validated by pure regex+calendar arithmetic — NO Date/clock at all, so a hostile value cannot destabilize the digest; the contract comment records that freshness re-observation is the consumer's duty per design 810. Digest covers every field via sorted-key canonical serialization; tests prove identical sha256 across runs and input key orders, and a changed field always changes the digest. Attribution: dirty/staged/untracked/unmerged/ignored/clean plus ABSENT and UNKNOWN. Three deviations from the plan's letter, all fail-closed and tested: (a) added ScopePathObserver as a second injected port — realpath/exists are needed for symlink containment and cannot come from the git port; (b) added submodulePaths() as a fifth GitObserver method — an unchanged submodule never appears in porcelain v2, so the boundary is not otherwise observable; (c) added UNMERGED and ABSENT to the class list — both are genuinely classifiable, so folding them into UNKNOWN would have been dishonest, and UNKNOWN is now reserved for real contradictions (a `1 .. ...` record claiming a change with no change) rather than being a catch-all. Adapter copies the testkit phase0-node-git discipline wholesale (safe.directory, core.fsmonitor=false, core.untrackedCache=false, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=NUL on win32, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, LC_ALL=C, buffer encoding + fatal UTF-8, porcelain v2 -z, no shell, 30s timeout, 8 MiB maxBuffer) and maps ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER to RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_OVERFLOW. The base environment is an explicit parameter (hermeticGitEnvironment(base)) rather than an ambient process.env read, which keeps production sources free of process.env for the step-6 determinism gate — verified: the only hit in packages/runner/src is the integration test. One integration test builds a real repo under os.tmpdir() with skipIf(no git) and confirms CLEAN/DIRTY/UNTRACKED/IGNORED end to end; it removes its fixture in a finally block.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red then green — src/workspace/workspace-manifest.test.ts + src/workspace/workspace-manifest.ts (design 218-219/485/491/817). buildInputManifest({baseIdentity, entries}) where EVERY entry is {path, sha256, byteLength, producer} and producer is typed { kind: "BASE" } | { kind: "PREDECESSOR", attemptRef, epoch, adoptionRef? } — producer identity MUST live in the input manifest (BLOCKER from verification: a sha256 is one-way, producer identity is uncomputable from a digest; design 218 requires producer attempts/epochs/adoptions + inherited-path ownership) -> frozen digest-bound manifest, sorted canonical entries. buildResultManifest({inputManifest (the FULL object, not just its digest), scopeObservation, authoredPaths, resultTreeEntries, declaredArtifactRefs}) validates fail-closed with DISTINCT stable RUNNER_WORKSPACE_* codes: escaped (path outside canonical scope), symlinked/junction (from scope observation), FOREIGN (defined precisely: result-tree bytes attributable to NEITHER the inherited input closure NOR an in-scope authored path — no declared producer), dirty/staged/untracked (git-attribution states from the embedded scope observation), undeclared (result entry absent from authoredPaths+inherited closure), authored-path-out-of-scope, inherited-path producer mismatch (result inherited entry whose bytes/digest differ from its input-manifest producer entry). DIGEST BINDING IS EXPLICIT: the serialized result-manifest bytes EMBED inputManifest.sha256, scopeObservation.sha256, baseIdentity, sorted authored paths, sorted result-tree entries, and the inherited-versus-authored split — all inside the bytes producing the manifest sha256 (DoD 2: base, scope observation, input tree, authored paths, result tree all digest bound — transitively through embedded digests). Reproducibility tests: same inputs -> byte-identical manifest + digest across runs and key orders. DEFERRED FIELDS (explicit deferral, name it in a contract comment so QA sees intent vs design 219): authored commit/canonical delta, receipts, decisions, journal references belong to the later result-sealing task; this module builds the tree/ownership/digest core. RED first, then green; src/index.ts exports public surface of all three areas.

(2) Digest recompute is wrapped: a manifest or observation that cannot even be canonically serialized (e.g. an `adoptionRef: undefined` hand-built entry) is treated as unsealed rather than throwing out of the builder. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Rename-over-existing for duplicate content — REJECTED after empirical verification on this machine (Node v24.16.0 win32): renameSync silently REPLACES a closed existing destination (would mask corruption at an address) and throws EPERM when a reader holds it open; protocol is check-exists -> verify-existing -> drop-temp, rename only onto nonexistent addresses. (2) writeFileSync-based staging — impossible: no fd, so fsync-before-rename is unimplementable; port is fd-oriented. (3) fsync(file) as the durability point — insufficient: rename metadata is not durable without POSIX parent-dir fsync / win32 reopen-and-flush; persistAfterRename is a first-class injectable fault boundary and the ref returns only after it. (4) Producer identity looked up from digests at result time — impossible (one-way); input-manifest entries carry mandatory typed producer (BASE | PREDECESSOR{attemptRef, epoch, adoptionRef}) per design 218. (5) Depending on @moe/testkit for the git adapter — rejected (phase0-scoped package); the execFile discipline is copied wholesale locally. (6) fast/random temp names — rejected (determinism rail); injected counter entropy. Plan verified by 2-agent workflow (design/fs skeptic, mechanics skeptic); 1 BLOCKER + 6 RISKs folded in.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Design anchors: 932 (staging: written->flushed->renamed->verified->referenced; uncertain reference prevents deletion), 208/810/812 (ScopeResolutionObservation fields; case/symlink/junction/submodule/device/UNC/absolute/escape fail-closed; git attribution = changed paths + before/after trees + dirty/staged/untracked manifests), 218-219/485/491 (input manifest carries producer attempts/epochs/adoptions + inherited-path ownership; result manifest = input digest/tree, authored delta, result tree, inherited-vs-authored split; no foreign staged/untracked smuggling), 817 (clean-candidate rejection list: dirty, staged, untracked, symlinked, escaped, undeclared). testkit phase0-node-git.ts is the proven Windows git-spawn discipline: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL='NUL' on win32, safe.directory, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 (index.lock churn in this multi-agent tree), fsmonitor/untrackedCache off, buffer encoding + fatal UTF-8, porcelain v2 -z; maxBuffer overflow is a hard ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER error (fail-closed) — map to stable code. Lockfile live state at planning time: packages/skills untracked + its importer already in working-tree pnpm-lock.yaml; packages/core not yet present; ordering rule in steps 1/7. tsBuildInfoFile must be runner.tsbuildinfo.
planningNotes.risks: (1) Poisoned content address: post-rename verify failure MUST unlink/quarantine before returning, or the true content can never stage again — test asserts empty address. (2) Lockfile ordering: committing pnpm-lock.yaml while a foreign importer's package.json is uncommitted breaks --frozen-lockfile for everyone; runner commits LAST among current greenfield tasks. (3) Windows rename semantics differ from POSIX in both directions (silent replace vs EPERM-under-reader) — the exists-check-first protocol handles both; AV scanners can hold handles, so EPERM on rename maps to the verify-existing fallback, not a crash. (4) 'ignored' git class requires an explicit lsFilesIgnored call — default porcelain v2 cannot produce it; unclassifiable stays UNKNOWN, never clean. (5) observedAt is caller-supplied — validate format so a hostile timestamp cannot destabilize the observation digest; freshness is the consumer's re-observation duty (design 810), documented. (6) Deferred result-manifest fields (authored commit/delta, receipts, decisions, journal refs) are an EXPLICIT deferral vs design 219 — the contract comment must say so or QA can reject. (7) Shared dirty tree: skills/core/store tasks in flight; attribute red repo gates before acting; no scratch files (auto-commit sweep).
